A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Certified Circuits, with matching authors, framework, and identifiable retained experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ResNet experiments measuring circuit accuracy, size, non-target-class accuracy, and structural stability on ImageNet and four OOD datasets.

after.justification: v3 reports original vision and language experiments, including circuit performance, seed stability, radius sensitivity, feature visualizations, and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 extend the vertex-based formulation to edge masks, adding construction of circuits from certified edges and their incident vertices. The deletion sampling, inclusion probabilities, and threshold-and-abstain rule remain unchanged. This is a limited procedural extension of the existing wrapper.

E1.justification: v3 retains ImageNet and the four vision OOD datasets and adds language evaluation on IOI, IOI-Hard, and Greater-Than. These introduce indirect-object and year-prediction tasks, with distinct OOD conditions involving object/place distractors, repeated question-and-answer detours, and pre-answer distractors (Appendix B.2).

E2.justification: The three vision comparators—relevance, activation, and rank top-K—remain. v3 adds evaluated EAP-IG baselines for language and a majority-vote comparator using the same 1,000 deletion samples for vision (Appendix F.5). The latter directly tests whether certification adds value beyond ensemble averaging.

E3.justification: New protocols include ViT-B/16 and GPT-2 Small evaluation, language splits of 100 discovery, 100 ID-test, and 100 OOD-test prompts, exact next-token accuracy, and task-specific certification-parameter sweeps. Additional experiments vary concept-set size and certified radius. The non-target-class oACC evaluation is removed; the main vision certification defaults remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 retains cross-distribution circuit-IoU analysis and adds independent-seed stability, radius-versus-data-size sensitivity, a matched-compute majority-vote control, runtime analysis, and expanded feature case studies (Appendices D–F). Conversely, v1 Appendix C's quantitative class-specificity analysis using non-target images is absent.

E5.justification: v1 reports certification confidence but no comparable empirical uncertainty or seed study. v3 Table 5 adds plus/minus uncertainty and paired class-level significance tests; Appendix F.2 reports 40 independent seeds and a 95% confidence interval for mean IoU. Appendix C.3 explicitly specifies Bonferroni family-wise error control. The certification sampling budget remains 1,000.

E6.justification: Retained results change: ResNet-101 relevance-based ImageNet peak cACC is 96% certified versus 86% baseline in v1 Table 1, versus 95% and 83% in v3 Table 1. v3 also adds language, ViT, runtime, and sensitivity results; language ID circuits match 100% baseline accuracy with substantially fewer edges. oACC results disappear. Revised vision numbers do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A change the certified neighborhood from edit distance < r to ≤ r, while definitions expand to edge components. Appendix C.2 adds a perfect-agreement sample-complexity analysis with simultaneous certification. The central radius formula and RS-Del proof strategy remain; the proof still concludes invariance of the non-abstaining smoothed label.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains an algorithm-agnostic framework for dataset-level circuit stability. The abstract and contribution summary expand the explicitly claimed empirical validation to vision and language and revise headline benefits from up to 91% higher accuracy and 45% fewer neurons to 56% higher accuracy and 80% fewer components, distinguishing language compactness from vision accuracy gains.

C2.justification: Section 6 replaces the linear-runtime limitation with a caching-based account supported by approximately 2.4× ResNet overhead. New interpretations distinguish language accuracy plateaus from vision curves, attribute benefits beyond averaging to abstention, and identify concept-set size as a constraint on larger radii. Future-work boundaries shift from ViTs and language generally to larger language, multimodal, and sparse-activation models.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents vision discovery/evaluation overlap, 50 validation images per class, corruption severity, model sources, ViT hooks, language prompts and graph construction, certification pseudocode, caching, and runtime hardware (Appendices B–D). It replaces the promise of future code with a repository link, whose availability is not established by the PDFs. Newly disclosed vision settings do not establish experimental changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting EAP/EAP-IG, Greater-Than, GPT-2, ViT, implementation libraries, and recent vision-transformer circuit work. The main positioning against dataset instability and input-level verification remains. The Anonymous-to-Hadad citation update and publication-metadata revisions identify retained work rather than new research relationships.

P1.justification: The abstract, experimental setup, and results narrative are substantially rewritten around parallel vision/language comparisons and component-level terminology. Feature visualization becomes a separate main-text subsection, while the three-scorer comparison moves into the appendix. Appendices are reorganized into experimental setup, certification analysis, runtime, language results, and vision results.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the overview and pipeline figures, restructures Table 1 into a multimodal comparison, and simplifies the main vision curve grid. It adds language circuit diagrams, uncertainty tables, seed and radius plots, runtime displays, and feature panels. The original radius plot and structural-stability plot remain in revised presentations; the oACC table is removed.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the previously CNN-only empirical case through language and ViT evaluation, a majority-vote control, seed uncertainty, and radius/data-size studies. Detailed estimation procedures and measured runtime also address important reproducibility and practicality gaps. Removing oACC weakens quantitative specificity evidence, and the pre-existing mismatch between the thresholded-output theorem and the non-abstaining-label proof remains. Nevertheless, the added empirical scrutiny and technical documentation provide a substantial net improvement.
